text:
oncall-ai: ALERT: sudden spike of CUDA OOM on gpu-serve-prod-7. Multiple containers restarting. Paging eng-runtime + eng-sre.
oncall-ai: incident created INC-2026-0428 (P1). Paging primary oncall.
elaine: Im on it. Saw the first OOM at 03:12 UTC. Node reports plenty of driver free memory but app-level OOM from allocator. Containers crashlooping ~45s.
raj: Paste from logs:
```
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.1 GiB (GPU 0; total 48.00 GiB; free 18.45 GiB; reserved 28.00 GiB)
  at /usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/csrc/cuda/Stream.cpp:...
```
raj: Reserved=28GB is suspicious for these small-serving containers. Looks like caching allocator reserved a lot.
marta: Noted deploy from yesterday included PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:32 for throughput. Could be increasing fragmentation.
eng-runtime-bot: deploybot: image redwood/serve:v2026.04.27 deployed yesterday to prod, config include custom allocator flags.
elaine: Immediate mitigation: redirect canary traffic off gpu-serve-prod-7, cordon node, start graceful drain. Scaling up replicas on gpu-serve-prod-2/4 to absorb load.
raj: For debugging I ran:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-serve-prod-7
kubectl drain gpu-serve-prod-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=5m
ssh gpu-serve-prod-7 'sudo systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced; sudo pkill -f serve || true'
```
elaine: After killing containers and restarting persistenced, some containers recovered but a few still throw OOM when allocating ~6-8GB. Driver free shows >15GB.
marta: Reminder: host pagecache drop does NOT free CUDA allocator reserved blocks. Need restart of processes or GPU daemon to release.
customer-bot: Customer impact: 12 customer clusters saw ~6% error rate in embeddings and streaming endpoints between 03:12-03:28 UTC. Lowest tier customers hit timeouts.
raj: Hypothesis: two things happening: 1) allocator fragmentation from small-split allocations + small max_split_size_mb causing many reserved blocks, 2) reserved memory from prior model loads not freed due to process reuse / in-process caches.
elaine: Quick config change pushed to canary: set PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128 for 2 replicas and lower per-worker concurrency by 25%. Deploying now.
eng-runtime-bot: deploybot: canary config roll (sha: a1d9f2c) to 2 replicas started 03:22 UTC.
marta: Also temporarily enabling fallback routing: if allocator_free < 8GB for a replica, route to smaller model variant. Added soft throttle on batched requests.
elaine: After canary changes and node drain, error rate dropped to ~0.7% by 03:30 UTC. Holding traffic shifts for 30m to ensure stability.
raj: Next steps for postmortem: capture caching allocator stats (torch.cuda.memory_reserved, memory_allocated, empty_cache calls), add exporter metric for reserved vs driver free, and gather dlmalloc / allocator fragmentation profiles.
marta: Ops actions: add alert when reserved / driver_free > 0.6 for > 2mins; add runbook step to restart nvidia-persistenced + full container runtime recreation (not just restart) when allocator mismatch persists.
eng-sre: Also audit GPU node processes for non-redwood consumers. We saw a background video-transcode job on a different node before; ensure nodes are single-tenant for serving pools.
elaine: Leaving node cordoned and replicas shifted. Ill monitor until 05:00 UTC and then handoff to night oncall. If OOMs reappear, escalate and schedule host reboot.
oncall-night: ack, will take handoff at 05:00 UTC. Keep thread updated with any allocator traces collected.
deploy-bot: note: canary config rolled back to stable for 5% traffic at 03:35 UTC after validation (sha: a1d9f2c).
elaine: Added immediate todo: collect gdb / python trace on one of the failing containers if it fails again, and dump torch allocator stats to S3.
raj: Longer term: consider moving to arena-based eviction policy, or exposing allocator defrag APIs if available. Also evaluate using NCCL / CUDA settings to reduce reserved block overhead.
marta: Recording incident actions in INC-2026-0428. Postmortem owners: eng-runtime (lead: raj), eng-sre (lead: marta).
elaine: Thanks everyone. Customer impact mitigated by traffic migration and canary config. Leaving logs and core dumps in INC-2026-0428 attachments. Will follow up with postmortem writeup tomorrow.
